question:
(i) Obtain the expression for the speed of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom.
(ii) Compare the speeds of the electron in the first and third Bohr orbits.
(iii) Explain the physical reason for the change in speed with increasing orbit number.

options.A: Using Bohr’s model, $v_n=\frac{e^2n}{2\varepsilon_0h}$. Hence $v_1:v_3=1:3$, because electrons move faster in higher orbits.
options.B: Using the electrostatic force condition with $mvr=\frac{nh}{2\pi}$ gives $v_n=\frac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_0hn}$. Thus $v_n\propto\frac1n$, so $v_1:v_3=3:1$. In higher orbits the electron is farther from the nucleus, the electrostatic attraction is weaker, and a smaller speed is required.
options.C: The speed is independent of $n$, so $v_1=v_3$, because all Bohr orbits have the same kinetic energy.
options.D: $v_n=\frac{h}{2\pi mnr}$, so $v_1:v_3=9:1$ because radius increases as $n^2$.
